name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: 5-6 Sep direct ballistic-missile fire on a U.S. carrier and destroyer; CENTCOM disabled/destroyed three Iranian tankers; Iran struck three more tankers plus U.S.-linked vessels and claimed (unconfirmed) an attack on a U.S. unmanned surface vessel; Iran threatens a 'faster, heavier, more painful' response.
importance: Critical — the sharpest escalation of the reignited U.S.-Iran conflict, with force-protection, munitions, and global-oil-market implications.
assessment: Calculated, reciprocal escalation rather than a bid for full-scale war, but the demonstrated willingness to fire ballistic missiles at U.S. warships plus an explicit retaliation threat materially raises miscalculation risk.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — no further confirmed exchanges since the 6 Sep tanker strikes; Iran's retaliation threat remains unresolved.
orgRelevance: Reassess Hormuz-transit shipping, personnel, and supply-chain exposure; energy-cost and freight-routing contingency planning.
nextIndicator: Whether Iran follows through on its retaliation threat; any strike on a U.S.-flagged or clearly U.S.-linked vessel; oil-price trajectory.

history.note: Operation Epic Fury begins the current conflict cycle.
Ceasefire collapses; Iran begins targeting Hormuz shipping.
IRGC fires ballistic missiles at a U.S. carrier and destroyer (both evade); CENTCOM disables/destroys three Iranian tankers.
IRGC Navy strikes three more tankers and three U.S.-linked vessels; claims (unconfirmed) an unmanned-vessel attack; Iran threatens harsher retaliation.

name: CMMC Implementation
status: Phases 2–4 suspended (13 Jul 2026) pending a 60-day review; internal findings to the DoW CIO targeted ~13 Sep 2026 (under a week away), public report ~28 Sep; DFARS 252.204-7012/7021, SPRS scores, and annual affirmations remain in force.
importance: High — governs DIB compliance spend and contract-award eligibility.
assessment: Policy pause, not repeal; a reformed program and reset timeline remain the leading outcome, with the internal decision window now imminent.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — no substantive new information; ~13 Sep internal deadline now under a week away.
orgRelevance: Maintain 800-171 controls, SPRS currency, and C3PAO readiness; move from monitoring to final-readiness posture.
nextIndicator: DoW CIO internal determination ~13 Sep; Federal Register notice or public report ~28 Sep.

history.note: DFARS acquisition rule effective; 252.204-7021/7025 added.
DoD suspends CMMC Phases 2–4 pending 60-day review.
Pause continues; safeguarding + SPRS obligations unchanged.
Internal DoW CIO findings targeted ~13 Sep, now under a week away; no substantive change to the pause.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's military-affiliated license-denial rule (since 1 Dec 2025) is compounded by June 2026 entity-list additions specifically naming U.S. rare-earth developers MP Materials and USA Rare Earth among ten defense-linked firms; DoD funding domestic mine-to-magnet capacity.
importance: Critical — binding, now more surgically targeted, constraint on munitions/platform output and the domestic-substitution response itself.
assessment: Durable, weaponizable chokepoint escalated from broad licensing restriction to targeted entity-list action against the specific firms building Western alternatives; structural risk HIGH, near-term program impact MODERATE-to-HIGH given the direct targeting.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — confirmed June 2026 entity-list action specifically names MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
orgRelevance: Map magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities; pursue second sources outside China-targeted firms.
nextIndicator: DoD mine-to-magnet award cadence and FORGE-initiative disbursement; any further PRC entity-list or licensing action.

history.note: China imposes rare-earth export controls on 7 of 17 elements.
License denial extended to military-affiliated foreign firms.
China adds ten U.S. entities to its dual-use export control list, including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
Continued strain; DoD invests in domestic capacity.
Confirmed the June entity-list action specifically targets domestic rare-earth substitution firms, escalating the chokepoint's severity.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / AI-Infra CVEs
status: CISA added 7 KEV CVEs (2 Sep) + Chromium V8 (4 Sep) incl. SonicWall SMA1000, JFrog Artifactory, LiteLLM; no further KEV adds confirmed since. Independent researchers separately report active exploitation of MikroTik RouterOS, ASUS Control Center Enterprise, and a Magento/Adobe Commerce zero-day, none yet KEV-listed.
importance: High — trust-boundary and transaction-platform components common in enterprise and DIB networks.
assessment: Attacker focus on identity, software supply chain, network infrastructure, and AI infrastructure continues; exploitation reported across both the formal KEV cohort and newly surfaced unlisted flaws.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — no new KEV adds since 4 Sep; new independent reporting on MikroTik/ASUS/Magento active exploitation outside KEV.
orgRelevance: Patch and threat-hunt the KEV cohort now; proactively mitigate MikroTik/ASUS/Magento ahead of formal listing; verify DFARS 7012 safeguarding evidence.
nextIndicator: KEV listing of MikroTik/ASUS/Magento CVEs; further KEV adds; defense-sector intrusion reporting.

history.note: Seven KEV additions (SonicWall, JFrog, LiteLLM, others).
Chromium V8 type-confusion added to KEV.
No new KEV adds; researchers report active exploitation of MikroTik RouterOS, ASUS Control Center Enterprise, and a Magento/Adobe Commerce zero-day, not yet KEV-listed.

name: Golden Dome Procurement
status: ~$1.75B for 36 SDA tracking satellites + up to $3.2B in space-based-interceptor awards; SHIELD IDIQ active; Commercial Solutions Opening open through 2031; pre-year-end 2026 SBI ground/flight testing and 2027 orbital demonstrations remain the near-term milestones.
assessment: Transitioned from funding to procurement; incumbents on SDA/MDA vehicles advantaged; the pre-2027 SBI test is the key near-term proof point, with no confirmation or slippage identified yet.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — no new award or testing-milestone news this cycle (holiday-affected publication window).

nextIndicator: SBI ground/flight test outcomes; further SDA Tranche launches; interceptor prototype milestones.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy
status: 3-day Kyiv–Moscow capital-strike pause (5 Sep) gave way to a 7 Sep Trump-Putin call producing a reported 30-day halt on strikes against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, contingent on Ukrainian reciprocity; Trump then held an hour-long call with Zelensky; no comprehensive ceasefire.
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand.
assessment: A narrower, potentially more durable, category-bounded commitment than the prior capital-strike pause; frontline tempo remains unaffected pending confirmation the commitment holds.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — Trump-Putin call yields the reported 30-day energy-infrastructure halt commitment; Ukrainian reciprocity not yet confirmed.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; no direct organizational action.
nextIndicator: Confirmation of Ukrainian reciprocity; any reported violation of the energy-infrastructure halt.

history.note: Temporary 3-day capital-strike halt; Putin rejects frontline ceasefire; ZNPP local ceasefire for repairs.
Trump-Putin call produces a reported 30-day energy-infrastructure strike-halt commitment contingent on Kyiv reciprocity; Trump-Zelensky call follows.

name: China–Taiwan Pressure / Trump-Xi Summit
status: MND 2026 report flags PLA landing-capability buildup; sustained CCG gray-zone activity. A 24 Sep Trump-Xi White House visit remains the U.S.-side plan (invited at the May Beijing summit); no fresh Chinese confirmation identified this cycle.
importance: High — Indo-Pacific deterrence, FMS, interoperability, and the broader U.S.-China relationship.
assessment: Capability investment plus gray-zone normalization continues independent of the diplomatic track; the floated summit keeps rare-earth and Taiwan friction points in play simultaneously, with low expectations for major deliverables.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — no new Taiwan-specific development; summit date stands on the U.S. side without fresh Chinese confirmation.
orgRelevance: Reinforces maritime ISR, undersea, counter-amphibious, resilient PNT demand; Indo-Pacific- and rare-earth-dependent programs should watch the pre-summit period.
nextIndicator: Formal Chinese confirmation of the 24 Sep visit; any large named PLA exercise; pre-summit rare-earth or Taiwan movement.

history.note: Taiwan MND 2026 report to Legislative Yuan emphasizes PLA landing capability.
24 Sep Trump-Xi White House visit remains the U.S.-side plan; no fresh Chinese confirmation identified.

name: DoD Leadership Continuity
status: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned (2 Sep); Adam Telle named acting Army Secretary; Sean Parnell (Hegseth ally) has emerged as the leading contender for the permanent post among at least four candidates.
importance: Medium — policy-continuity risk during the CMMC review, reprogramming cycle, and active CENTCOM operations.
assessment: The acting appointment reduces near-term disruption; the permanent pick's identity will signal whether Driscoll's modernization agenda continues or is redirected toward alignment with Secretary Hegseth.
lastChange: 2026-09-07 — Adam Telle named acting Secretary; Sean Parnell reported as leading contender for the permanent role.
orgRelevance: Monitor for Army acquisition-priority shifts; watch the permanent nominee's confirmation posture.
nextIndicator: Formal nomination of a permanent Army Secretary; SASC confirmation-hearing scheduling.

history.note: NPR reports Driscoll resignation amid clashes with the Defense Secretary.
Adam Telle named acting Army Secretary; Sean Parnell emerges as leading contender for the permanent post.
